decisions.summary: plan_site takes spec.windward or DEFAULT_WINDWARD ('NW'); windward_for and WIND_TURNS deleted; HamletSpec.windward is the declaration; the manifest records wind_source = declared | regional.
decisions.why: Unchanged. FR-001, FR-002, FR-003, FR-007 and the request ('only when declared as the default').

decisions.summary: seat_cluster refuses a margin whose outward normal is more than 45 degrees off the wind (WIND_BACK_MIN_DOT = cos 45).
decisions.why: Unchanged. FR-004 states the 45-degree bar itself.

decisions.summary: A margin under the bar is used only when no wind-facing margin exists; recorded as meta.seat_offwind; forbidden on every pool map by the pool test.
decisions.why: Unchanged ruling. With the strike-out retired, the only things left that refuse every wind-facing margin are the seat's hard constraints (drain, wet toe), which FR-010 keeps and the record supports. Where they refuse every such margin, the literal rule is physically impossible, and the only alternative, renaming the wind, is the behavior the GM asked to end. The fallback never renames the wind, is recorded on the map, and is forbidden on the pool, so FR-004's pool clause holds. The debt from the previous review is paid: T21 records the count on the amended engine, 3 of 48 cohort seeds off-wind. The GM gets that number in the hand-off.

decisions.summary: Order is clean wind-facing, then off-wind; feature 230's strike-out retired; a margin the brook crosses is scored down by 3.0 x the share of band points near the brook; the across-the-water failure moves to D10.
decisions.why: The GM's 2026-09-27 ruling and FR-012 (no refusal when a crossing can be drawn). A penalty is a preference, not a refusal. The previous wording nit ('per crossing') is fixed and now matches the code.

decisions.summary: Inashiro 4, Kuwabata 21, Kashikawa 3, Mizuguchi 23 kept; Sawada 6 -> 24 on the drain and wet toe; the pool test holds bearing and a 200-degree arc.
decisions.why: Exactly the amended Edge Case and SC-008. No seed is moved to route around the engine. Re-read 2026-09-28 after the wording fix: the plan now marks 'astride its brook (8 and 4)' as R7's measurement at seed 23 and states that D18's belt-room tier later seats all 12 on one bank - a seat moved for belt room, not refused for the brook (FR-012 holds). Class unchanged.

decisions.summary: windbreak_default(meta) states the belt's side and whether the wind is regional or declared; class What drops 'high side'; Entry names vegetation/030.
decisions.why: Unchanged. FR-008, US3.

decisions.summary: vegetation/030 rewritten to the rule as built with re-measured arcs; gloss corrected; hamletgen.md, indexes, five notes files.
decisions.why: Unchanged. FR-009, US4.

decisions.summary: brook_banks() fixed the divided test, then was retired with the strike-out; bank_of() remains.
decisions.why: Unchanged. A consequence of D3 that narrows nothing.

decisions.summary: Kashikawa bamboo=both, Mizuguchi byre_form=courtyard and copse_siting=against_the_belt, Sawada lane_web=alleys stay declared; HamletSpec.byre_form added.
decisions.why: Unchanged. The request's only 'declared' constraint is the wind, which stays undeclared. These declarations pin values the maps showed before and touch neither the wind nor the seat.

decisions.summary: brook_fords every 160 ft where the brook bends under 20 degrees; a 30 ft corridor gap each side of each ford; the spur routed through a ford; bridges() decks every crossing; far_bank, the strike-out and the brook re-roll deleted.
decisions.why: Unchanged. This is what the GM approved ('let ways cross the brook with a plank footbridge'), with FR-011 and FR-012. The spacing and bend limit are the guess the spec's Decisions row records (m:ford-spacing re-measured at 160).

decisions.summary: The route lattice charges BROOK_CROSSING_COST_FT (150 ft, a guess recorded in water/270) for entering the brook's band, and the string-pull may not undo a crossing the lattice avoided (Kashikawa's lane crossed and recrossed to reach a house on its own bank). The band is kept as brook points in a 20 px bucket grid.
decisions.why: FR-011 says a way MUST be able to cross 'where the layout needs it'. A price keeps crossings available and takes away only the needless ones, like R9's cross-and-back lane. Nothing is refused: a way that has to cross still crosses when every other route costs more. No household, field path or seat loses anything FR-012 guarantees. It is a defect fix on the maps this feature re-rolled (US6, constitution XIV). The 150 ft is a guess, and the plan says so.

decisions.summary: stage_crossings squares every crossing more than 10 degrees off square (square_crossings), in the record and the ink together, before bridges() lays the deck.
decisions.why: FR-011 requires every way to cross the brook 'squarely'. R9 records a crossing 52 degrees off square before the fix and 0 after, so the decision enforces the requirement itself. The 10-degree tolerance is calibration of 'squarely', not a carve-out.

decisions.summary: _parts_across_stream and across_the_brook refuse a part or fixture across a stream from its house; labeled a guess with an absence note in homesteads/250.
decisions.why: Unchanged. FR-013 as written, and a placement rule rather than a seat refusal.

decisions.summary: The dooryard copse within 90 ft of a farmhouse, the against-the-belt copse within 60 ft of a belt crown, the re-seat nudge included.
decisions.why: FR-014 and SC-010. The figure nit is fixed: the plan now says 393 crowns at a median of 167 ft (R8), and m:copse-house-reach re-measured at 90.

decisions.summary: Where the connector hands over to the lanes, that junction is the entrance anchor. departure_routes walks every dwelling's way out through the lanes to the handover and out along the connector. Both placers keep first the seats the fewest routes miss (routes_missed, 20 ft), then those within KOSATSUBA_HANDOVER_BAND_FT (20 ft) of the handover, and the connector is offered as a way to post on. The census counts ways out that pass an entrance board. A connector that meets no other way keeps the first-arrival walk.
decisions.why: FR-015 says, word for word, 'on the way the connector meets, within the entrance band - so every departure passes it'. The handover is the one point every departure passes, so this decision puts FR-015's own purpose into code rather than a proxy for it. 'Fewest missed' ranks the seats. It does not excuse a board that some routes miss: test_pool_261 asserts routes_missed == 0 on every entrance map. I checked the one possible silent exclusion, departure_routes skipping a dwelling more than 150 px from any lane. It routes every household on all five maps (15/15, 20/20, 16/16, 12/12, 19/19). The first-arrival case is a connector with no other way to meet: there the connector is the only way, so FR-015's anchor clause has no junction to name. The census change serves FR-018, since the notes now state what the board is sited for.

decisions.summary: unfold deletes a brook vertex turning more than 100 degrees.
decisions.why: Unchanged. FR-017, SC-013.

decisions.summary: The pool test holds every 40 ft bin to 30 ft of depth except bins a way or the brook runs through and bins the page edge cuts.
decisions.why: Unchanged ruling, each case judged on its own: the page edge truncates what can be measured; trees cannot stand in the brook, which the GM's ruling puts through the place; a way crossing the belt has to part it. The spec's own Decisions row carries the same carve-out, and the earlier measurement found nothing thin hidden in the exempted bins.

decisions.summary: The pop-up says the belt stands 'toward the northwest'; the class text says 'on the windward one or two sides'.
decisions.why: Unchanged. FR-008 read together with FR-016's second clause.

decisions.summary: The spur's origin stops on the houses' bank, short of a stream it would cross; the spur is scored against the brook gapped at the fords; trim_lane_stubs leaves the spur to the sweeps that record a drop; the dangling-ends sweep counts the dry hem, as well as the paddy, as the field.
decisions.why: FR-012 ('at least one way reaches the field') and SC-008 ('every hamlet whose field is across the brook has a way that reaches it'). Each of the three fixes removes something that stopped the engine from drawing the crossing the GM's ruling asks for: fix the algorithm, not the seat. On the dry hem: the hem plots are worked ground of the same field (the spec's Edge Case names them as cropland beside 'the crop'), and a path ending at the field's cultivated hem has reached the field on a plain reading. test_pool_261 test_a_way_reaches_the_field holds a way within 60 ft of the paddy or the hem on every map whose field lies across the brook. Wording nit: the plan says each of the three maps gets 'its one way to the rice', but Mizuguchi's spur stops at the hem, which the code comment puts 108 ft from the paddy outline. 'To the field' is the accurate phrase. Re-read 2026-09-28: the only change is "rice" -> "field" (the dry hem counts as the field), which matches FR-012 "at least one way reaches the field".

decisions.summary: ford_crossing, path_violations (the brook term and the twice-bridged count) and the first square_crossings used seg_intersect (a line test) as a segment-crossing test; each now tests segments_cross first; the connector bearings changed on four maps, and the notes' district directions were re-read from the drawn tracks.
decisions.why: A constitution XIV defect fix found in this work. It narrows nothing: it removes false crossings that pushed every spur to a ford and scored violations on connectors. The re-read district directions serve FR-018.

decisions.summary: brook_skirt turns the brook off the frame where the frame box would pin it, after half its stations; Sawada's 457 ft ruled along the top margin is now 66 ft, held by a pool test that fires on the old manifest.
decisions.why: A settlement-review finding on a map this feature re-rolled (US6, SC-014), measured against the GM's own standing 2026-08-26 ruling. m:sawada-brook-ruled re-measured at 457 (the old manifest's value, which the test fires on). The test only fails when the ruled run is present, so it enforces the request rather than adding scope.

decisions.summary: A non-round cluster shape is recorded as honored only past round's aspect ceiling (2.0). Inashiro's rolled crescent, drawn at 1.97, is now recorded meta.cluster_shape_unhonored.
decisions.why: FR-018: declarations must match what the map draws. Inashiro's manifest claimed a crescent that the map draws as a round cloud, and the recording mechanism for an unhonored rolled shape already existed (Kashikawa since 2026-08-16). The decision closes the 1.9-2.0 overlap that let a round drawing claim to be a crescent. It is not the route-around the GM forbade: no seed, seat or declaration was changed to dodge the engine, and the shape is a rolled knob that the spec never required a map to honor. Hand-off point for the GM, not a block: before this feature Inashiro, the reference hamlet, drew its crescent honored (notes: drawn aspect 2.49-3.25). At the new wind-facing seat it draws a round cloud, and the pool now honors a non-round shape on no map (manifests: Inashiro, Kashikawa, Mizuguchi and Sawada unhonored, Kuwabata round). Whether the placer should be made to draw the rolled shape at a wind-facing seat is the GM's 'fix the placement algorithm' question, and they should see it.

decisions.summary: The scrub's settlement keep-out is the hull of the houses and farmstead parts grown by 44 ft, not the bbox of the house centers.
decisions.why: Review findings on re-rolled maps (Sawada's rectangular clearing, Kuwabata's privy in the scrub): US6, SC-014, constitution XIV.

decisions.summary: A board's caption is seated on the page when any seat allows.
decisions.why: A review finding (Kashikawa's caption clipped off the page): US6, SC-014.

decisions.summary: generate finishes each attempt into a stage beside the map and promotes only the kept one.
decisions.why: A constitution XIV defect in the tooling: the gate's census read a rejected Sawada attempt, which made FR-006's 'pass the full gate' unreliable. It changes no map and narrows nothing.

decisions.summary: The XII row now records T13 and T15's research passes, the two guesses with absence notes, and mizu-no-bunka-60 judged APPLICABLE-WITH-LIMITS.
decisions.why: The stale row the previous review flagged is fixed, and it matches T13 and T15's ticked boxes.

decisions.summary: Baseline 37/48 (R3), amended engine 38/48 (R5, T21), every failure also failing on the baseline; 0 farmstead parts across the brook on the cohort.
decisions.why: The spec's cohort Edge Case and SC-009.

decisions.summary: Defects fixed in the work (D7, make record, D10-D17); the wind never renamed; the two MODE 1 refusals and the GM's ruling recorded; the off-wind last resort raised with the GM.
decisions.why: Consistent with D2-D4 and D9-D17 as reviewed above.

decisions.summary: One dot product per margin; fords a short list cut into the corridor once; the crossing band kept once per roll in a 20 px bucket grid asked per lattice cell; D10 one segment test per part.
decisions.why: The new crossing price states how it is indexed (the bucket grid), as the project rule asks. It narrows nothing.

decisions.summary: No solid farmstead part, the house included, on a stream (_rect_on_stream); the board prefers an open seat among those every departure passes; a through connector hands over where a lane end meets it; the dangling-ends sweep runs again after straighten_joints.
decisions.why: Review findings on the re-rolled maps fixed in the placer (constitution XIV, US6, FR-013, FR-015). None narrows a clause of the request or the spec.

decisions.summary: A lane running back along another for 30 ft within 14 ft is cut where the doubling starts; the narrower tail is cut, never the wider; empty and one-point lane records dropped.
decisions.why: Drawing defects the reviews found (constitution XIV). No household loses its way: the cut is refused where a tail is some house's only way.

decisions.summary: An orphan join routes with the brook as an obstacle and refuses an even-count crossing except as a last resort; a household whose way out crosses the brook and back is served on its own bank (_link_home_bank), and the lane over the brook it no longer needs is dropped where every house it serves is served by the rest.
decisions.why: FR-011/FR-012 ask that ways MAY cross the brook where the layout needs it, decked; a crossing and straight back is not needed. The last resort keeps a household joined (FR-012 'every household reaches a way'), so nothing asked is given up.

decisions.summary: The siter and the frame re-seat ask feature 266's one placer whether the caption fits at the board's angle; a seat clear of the canopy ranks first; the level recorded.
decisions.why: Review findings (caption on a roof, a lane, the canopy) fixed by using main's placer; honors the GM's 2026-08-27 ruling that the caption stands at the board's angle. Narrows nothing asked.

decisions.summary: A lane crossing any drawn channel is squared like a brook crossing; a lane elbow inside the brook's half-width is dropped before squaring.
decisions.why: Extends FR-011's 'crosses it squarely' to the plank the research says crosses its ditch square (ways/030); a fix, not a narrowing.

decisions.summary: A roll that raises removes its own stage and .roll-*/ is ignored; a review acceptance counts only for the round it answered and a NOT-REVIEWABLE record keeps the verdict it was written over (scripts/_review_prereq.py).
decisions.why: Defects found in this work and fixed in it (constitution XIV). No effect on what a map draws.

decisions.summary: A third woodland parcel in a ruled line with two others is stepped sideways where ground allows and refused where it does not; Inashiro keeps 2 parcels; a parcel prefers a seat not across the field, a preference that falls back where no near-side seat qualifies inside the predicted frame.
decisions.why: The request and spec are silent on woodland parcels, so no clause is narrowed. Checked against the GM's standing ruling: the parcel count was already a target the scan meets only where there is ground (pre-feature parcels.py: 'a slot no size can seat is honestly dropped'), and a hamlet with two woodlots is itself a valid configuration, so this is not an engine failing to lay out a known-valid layout. The alternative kept was the recorded defect (the ruled chain).

decisions.summary: No copse clump based in the marsh (the copse alone; applied to every grove it cut Sawada's windward belt 179 -> 104 crowns, and 20-34 of 68 refused crowns stood on ground drawn dry because the toe marsh's recorded outline runs under cleared ground - deferred to future-work with measurement and sketch); a copse clump is near a house only on its own bank.
decisions.why: The copse keep-out is a new fix for a review finding (FR-014 family, constitution XIV); not extending it to the belt narrows nothing the GM or the spec asked, because the belt obeyed no marsh rule before this feature (pre-feature hinterland/belt.py has none), so FR-010's 'every rule the belt obeyed before' is intact. The marsh-outline defect is deferred with its measurement and sketch, the form XIV allows.

decisions.summary: A diagonal wind opens the belt's seating window on both axes; each arm has its own inner face (windbreak_faces); the frame holds every belt clump within 100 ft of a farmhouse on the page.
decisions.why: Makes the belt stand on the north AND west of the cluster for a NW wind (US1 scenario 3, SC-002); serves the request directly.

decisions.summary: A seat whose belt band would fall off the canvas scores down; a wind-facing seat whose band is more than a fifth off the canvas is a fallback below every wind-facing seat with room and above the off-wind ones.
decisions.why: Still inside FR-004's 45-degree bar: the new tier only orders wind-facing seats, and the off-wind fallback (D2) stays last and forbidden on the pool. It makes FR-006's 'windbreak on its cluster's northwest side' drawable on the page; it refuses no seat for the brook (FR-012).

decisions.summary: A belt stands its near face 12 ft beyond a lane that runs lengthwise inside its band (past_the_lanes), unless that would put the band's middle in the marsh; the band is not moved into the reeds' body, while crowns it already reaches at the reed edge are drawn as alder (D18l).
decisions.why: A new fix of Kuwabata's finding (a lane halving the drawn belt). The 'unless marsh' limits that new fix, not anything the request or spec asks: FR-016's floor is the record's 30 ft minimum (spec Decisions Recorded row), which the band keeps. Re-read 2026-09-28: the premise that conflicted with D18l is fixed - the plan now says the band is not moved INTO the reeds' body while its reed-edge crowns are alder, which agrees with D18l and the new spec Decisions row. Class unchanged.

decisions.summary: A front-row seat in the brook's corridor is pushed past the water (water_push) and, where the water moved it and it collides, tries a quarter pitch either way along the row.
decisions.why: Code read (homesteads/stages.py water_push): it pushes a seat's box clear of the water's clearance along the row normal; it refuses no seat for the brook and does not re-create the far-bank refusal, so FR-012 holds. It restored Inashiro's rolled crescent (a regression against main, constitution XIII).

decisions.summary: A windbreak crown seated in a toe marsh is drawn as alder; holding the belt off the reeds removed Sawada's windward belt and failed its depth test; the carr along the rest of the toe is not built.
decisions.why: This keeps the requested thing (a NW belt on every map, FR-006, on Sawada whose NW is its wet toe) rather than narrowing it; the belt had no marsh rule before (FR-010 intact). Not building the carr elsewhere narrows nothing asked. Re-read 2026-09-28: the Sawada figure is updated to 201 alder clumps (m:sawada-r17-alder, re-run: the notes line it greps is present) with the 70-of-201 figure marked as that round's; the spec now carries a Decisions row labeling the species accurate and the windbreak-on-marsh question a GUESS (R11). Class unchanged.

decisions.summary: The scrub keeps off each farmstead's grown outline and the ground between two within 140 ft, not the cluster's hull.
decisions.why: Review finding (a bare straight-edged wedge) fixed in the placer; constitution XIV.

decisions.summary: BROOK_WANDER_STEP 4 -> 10 and exit_bend; the segment leaving the tap run and the approach legs nudged off the screen axes; the scatter frame's prediction takes in the title pocket's band.
decisions.why: Drawing defects the reviews and the cohort found (constitution XIV, XIII); the GM's standing axis ruling honored. Narrows nothing asked.

decisions.summary: A household's own dry plot is laid against its homestead after the ways (the levee model), the canal hem kept as the second position; the plot's size a guess.
decisions.why: Review finding (Inashiro's dry plots a median 658 ft across the rice) fixed from the research (R11); constitution XIV. [2026-09-28: text unchanged, ruling kept; the mechanism is retired by D24.]

decisions.summary: The entrance is the outermost join walked in from the map's edge; a household's way out runs from its door to the connector's outer end; a lane run on past the connector to a loose end is cut unless it is some house's only way; _trim_to_service judges a lane end against every way but its own far end's.
decisions.why: FR-015 (every departure passes the board) measured honestly rather than by construction; fixes the lane-cut regressions the previous round made. No household loses its way.

decisions.summary: A bamboo stand keeps off the water at its half-width and 3 ft.
decisions.why: Review finding (culms on the brook); constitution XIV.

decisions.summary: An entrance board at a handover stands on the approach itself where a seat there passes every departure, squared to the way it stands on.
decisions.why: FR-015 and the research (broadside to the one way out).

decisions.summary: GRAIN_BOUGHT_IN: the mulberry dike-fishpond archetype lays no homestead grain plot (Kuwabata's GM-confirmed economy).
decisions.why: Makes the map match the GM's own canon (FR-018 family, constitution XIV); a review finding, not a narrowing. [2026-09-28: text unchanged, ruling kept; the mechanism is retired by D24.]

decisions.summary: A fixture is refused a seat across a lane from its house; a fixture with no recorded seat left gets the ring round its own house (a guess, labeled); a shrine with no seat passes to the next house with room, the count kept; the bundle box does not refuse the ring; the persimmon tries 10 and 20 ft further out and records a miss.
decisions.why: The GM's ruling applied as written: the new rule cost seven fixtures and two shrines, and the placer was fixed rather than the rule relaxed; 0 unseated on the pool. Narrows nothing asked.

decisions.summary: The far face is the fringe grown by a disc of the belt's depth sampled along the profile; the near face roughened only outward; the band laid 100 ft (D23).
decisions.why: FR-016 (the belt keeps its researched depth), fixing Kashikawa's hole and Sawada's bend at their cause.

decisions.summary: The brook's corners are filleted at 2.5 widths at the start of the crossings stage, the tap held, the planks squared against the rounded course; rounding at first draw was tried and reverted.
decisions.why: A drawing defect fixed (research: channels turn on curves). The request and spec say nothing it narrows; crossings stay square and decked (FR-011).

decisions.summary: The against-the-belt copse anchors on the belt's lee face, 0-60 ft leeward; meta.kosatsuba_well_ft records the board as drawn; the belt measured as one piece in crowns.
decisions.why: FR-014 ('at the belt's lee face, on the houses' side'), FR-018 (records match the map), FR-016.

decisions.summary: An alleys (accretion) hamlet's rank seats stand up to an eighth of a pitch off their exact rank; a back_lane (planned) hamlet's ranks stay regular, so Mizuguchi's lattice, the finding, is kept.
decisions.why: It leaves the review finding unfixed on the map it was found on, so it is an exception and is ruled. The previous spec-fidelity round refused keeping the lattice because the proposer never read the form and Sawada (alleys) drew the same lattice; both are now cured: the proposer reads the form and Sawada's ranks spread. What remains is the case the GM's own ruling names as legitimate - 'our research shows' - and the research does show it: research/homesteads 080 reads a back lane as a planning device giving 'a regular layout, right-angled development' (back-lane-enwiki, nucleated-village-enwiki, quoted in its notes). It keeps no behavior the GM asked to change and rests on no engine limitation.

decisions.summary: tidy_lane_ends reads the field as drawn, drops a lane trimmed to a point or a nub unless it is some house's only way, and runs as the web's last pass.
decisions.why: Fixes what main's re-laid pool exposed in the placer, per the GM's ruling; no household loses its way.

decisions.summary: round_the_houses adds near-face points every 30 ft and every 15 degrees round each house's disc windward of the chord; the band goes back to 100 ft; one piece on every map.
decisions.why: FR-016 and the belt's continuity (FR-010), fixed at the cause rather than covered by a deeper band.

decisions.summary: Where no side has room flush, the dry plot takes the nearest ground beside the steading, out from each lee or flank side and along it, never upwind, clear of the persimmon's trunk ring (a guess, labeled).
decisions.why: Fixes main's packed placer at the placer (the GM's ruling); never upwind keeps the belt's crop set-back (FR-010). [2026-09-28: text unchanged, ruling kept; the mechanism is retired by D24.]

decisions.summary: The fixture ring's last resort adds seats straight out from each wall; the persimmon's adds seats straight behind and before the house; all appended, so seated fixtures do not move.
decisions.why: 0 unseated on the pool; a placement fix, not a relaxation.

decisions.summary: The homestead grain plot (D18o, D19b's GRAIN_BOUGHT_IN, D23c) is removed with stage_homestead_fields, homesteads/fields.py, its fallback seats and its persimmon-ring reservation, after a search pass found no page placing a grain plot beside a house.
decisions.why: The request (northwest wind by default; fix the placement algorithm, not route around it) never asked for a homestead grain plot; the plot was the session's own addition under D18o. Removing it narrows nothing the GM asked for, and it executes the GM's explicit conditional instruction of 2026-09-28 (quoted by the caller: 'do that research pass and then if it's not supported, then go ahead and remove them'). The plan records the pass as finding no support (the grain-in-the-fields reading labeled a GUESS with an absence note), so the removal branch is the one the GM ordered. The fallback seats and persimmon reservation exist only to serve the plot and fall with it; GRAIN_BOUGHT_IN governed only the plot and is retired with it (spec row 269 marks it so).

decisions.summary: The dry crops stand in the comb's hem along the supply canal as on main; the research entry and the four dry-crop pop-ups say so, the grain-in-its-fields reading labeled a GUESS.
decisions.why: This is main's behavior restored, not a new carve-out, and it matches the model the GM's question named (dry crops on the higher ground just above the paddy water; the supply canal runs along the paddy's upper edge). The GM's 'if it is supported, add it to the write-up in the pop-up' branch did not fire; correcting the pop-ups so they no longer describe a removed plot is the record following the drawing.

decisions.summary: Inashiro's settlement-review finding (dry plots across the rice, median 658 ft) is answered by the record rather than the drawing; the pool test for a dry plot within 150 ft of the median house becomes a test that no grain plot stands by a house (0 on every map, m:dry-r24-retired).
decisions.why: The finding was a reviewer's, not the GM's request, and the GM's 2026-09-28 instruction decides it: with no support for a plot by the house, the plot is removed, and the distance the finding objected to is the direct consequence of that ruling. The inverted pool test only fails if the retired plot returns, so it enforces what the GM ordered rather than adding scope.

decisions.summary: Engine (D1-D3, D9-D17), measurement, pool, page, record, acceptance.
decisions.why: Sequencing only; D18-D23 are fixes found at acceptance and ride under phase 6's reviews.
